risk_reasons: Three transactional write sites inside deciding transactions that already hold a batch advisory lock and a batch row lock. A ledger failure aborts the decision it records.
The solicitation send path reaches real recipients. A defect in the ask or dispatch lane changes what a batch does, not only what it records.
Adds a second INSERT statement to src/lib/refusals/write.ts, which #1001 made the single owner of the refusal_events statement and its partial-index predicate.
goal: The three single-site solicitation lanes record a Refusal at decision time: ask_withheld in commitAskDecisions, outreach_withheld in commitWithhold, and batch_halted in latchHalt, each inside the transaction that made the decision.
non_goals: The outreach_withheld RENDER lane's four writers in ask-generation.ts. #1011 owns them, and they carry a different reason enum.
The held_draft and policy_gate_held lanes. #1013 owns them and #1004 put them last.
The Restraint tab and any read over refusal_events. #1014 owns the read path.
The five lane category maps. The feat/refusal-lane-vocabulary prerequisite lands them on main before this branch arms; this branch consumes them and edits vocabulary.ts for nothing.
Any migration. Migration 116 is applied to staging and production.
Backfilling Refusals decided before the ledger existed. #1002 ruled no backfill, ever.
Changing which candidates a batch withholds, which outreach the dispatch gate refuses, or which batches halt. This slice records those decisions and alters none of them.
user_visible_behavior: No owner-visible change. Nothing reads refusal_events until #1014.
A batch build writes one refusal_events row per withheld ask whose reason maps to a category, in the same transaction as the solicitation_asks insert.
A dispatch withhold writes one refusal_events row against the outreach id, in the same transaction as the withheld terminal.
An admin or platform halt writes one refusal_events row against the batch id. An owner halt writes none.
Setting REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false stops all three without a deploy and leaves ask, dispatch and halt behaviour byte-identical to today.
invariants: The ledger must never break the thing it records. Every write is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the partial index, and the new set-based arm re-spells refusal_events_subject_uniq's predicate byte-for-byte, identically to the single-row arm.

One statement per set. The ask lane writes N Refusals in one INSERT because a batch build can produce up to MAX_DATA_ROWS (5000) mapped Refusals while holding the batch advisory lock, reached when every candidate in the window fails an individual gate that maps to a category. Round 1 corrected an earlier MAX_DATA_ROWS-minus-BATCH_CAP figure, which describes the all-eligible case where the withholds are velocity_banked and write nothing.
src/lib/refusals/write.ts stays the only module that spells an INSERT INTO refusal_events. The set-based arm lives there, beside the single-row arm, and never in a lane module.

occurredAt is decision time at every site. The ask lane passes the batch's decidedAt, the dispatch lane passes the gate's own now, and the halt lane passes the transaction-time sentinel so occurred_at equals the halted_at the same NOW() wrote.
No site reads a timestamp back from Postgres and passes it forward as a JS Date. postgres.js truncates microseconds on decode.
A null category means the code is not a Refusal, so no row is written. velocity_banked, owner_veto, owner_halt, send_window_elapsed and batch_expired write nothing.
The halt lane writes exactly one Refusal per batch, never one per cancelled outreach. latchHalt copies one halt into N rows in one act.
Every row carries the account_id and business_id already in the lane's scope. No lane resolves a tenant key it does not hold.
A ledger failure is never caught at a call site. It aborts the deciding transaction, and the kill switch is the lever.
Tenant isolation: every row carries account_id NOT NULL and the table keeps deny-all RLS.
edge_cases: A batch build withholds every candidate in a 5000-row window with a MAPPED reason: one INSERT, not 5000 round trips under the advisory lock. The word mapped is load-bearing — the all-velocity_banked case below writes nothing at all, and an earlier wording of this line contradicted it.
A batch build withholds nothing: no statement is issued at all, because an INSERT with an empty row set is not a decision.
Every withheld ask in a build is velocity_banked: no statement is issued, for the same reason.
The same ask id is proposed twice inside one set-based INSERT: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING leaves one row and the statement still commits.
A rebuild re-evaluates the same contact: the ask id is newly minted per build, so the partial unique index does not collapse two builds into one Refusal. Each build is its own decision.
The dispatch gate defers rather than withholds: no Refusal, because a defer is a no-decision.
The dispatch lane's advisory lock blocks for seconds before the gate runs: occurred_at is the gate's clock, so the row is not stamped at transaction start.
A second halt of an already-halted batch: the CAS returns no row, latchHalt returns early, and no second Refusal is written.
The platform halt arm passes audit: null and writes no account_audit_log row: it still writes its Refusal, because the ledger write is its own statement.
An owner halts their own batch: no Refusal. RepWorth refused nothing.
REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is false: all three lanes complete their decisions unchanged and the helper emits one warning per disabled episode.
A CHECK violation from a writer bug aborts the batch build, the dispatch withhold or the halt, rolling back its audit row and outbox rows with it.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/auto-approval/suspension.ts — the #1009 call-site precedent: writeRefusalEvent on the deciding transaction, placed after the guard that proves a decision was made, with no try/catch.
src/lib/refusals/write.ts — the single-row arm this slice extends: the ON CONFLICT predicate, the occurredAtFragment sentinel, the kill-switch early return.

src/lib/solicitation/batch-builder.ts commitAskDecisions — the jsonb_to_recordset set-insert idiom the new arm follows, but NOT its affected-row-count assertion. That function has no ON CONFLICT, so count equals input there; under ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING a subject stored by an earlier call legitimately lowers the count and the assertion would throw inside a decision transaction.
src/lib/audit/log.ts writeAccountAuditLog — one helper owning one statement, the DB client as an explicit parameter.
src/lib/refusals/vocabulary.ts — the lane maps landed by the feat/refusal-lane-vocabulary prerequisite.
test_seams: src/lib/refusals/write.ts — writeRefusalEvent and the new set-based arm.
src/lib/solicitation/batch-builder.ts — buildSolicitationBatch, through which commitAskDecisions is reached.
src/lib/solicitation/dispatch.ts — the dispatch job entry point, through which commitWithhold is reached.
src/lib/solicitation/approval.ts — adminHaltBatch and the system halt entry point, both of which reach latchHalt.

src/lib/solicitation/approval.ts — haltBatch, the OWNER arm. It is the only entry point that produces owner_veto and owner_halt, so the exhaustive-reasons title cannot cover the two null-mapped owner cases without it.

rollback_plan: Three layers. (1) REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false on Railway stops every ledger write with no deploy and leaves ask, dispatch and halt behaviour byte-identical to today; invoke the flag-flip skill. (2) Revert the PR on main and redeploy, which removes the three call sites and the set-based arm together. (3) No down migration: migration 116 stays, and rows already written are not deleted by a revert. ArchivalPoller's refusal_events arm landed in #1009 and is not touched here, so surviving rows still age out at REFUSAL_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS.
observability: One warning per disabled episode from the helper whenever REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is false. It is the only signal that the ledger has a gap, because the ledger cannot show its own absence.

A ledger failure in the ask or dispatch lane reaches Sentry through attachJobFailureSink on the terminal BullMQ attempt, because both lanes run inside BullMQ workers. The admin halt lane is route-driven and surfaces as a failed request.

Reconciliation query for staging: COUNT(*) of refusal_events WHERE refusal_source = 'ask_withheld' must equal the count of solicitation_asks rows with a withheld_reason other than velocity_banked, per batch, inside the retention window.
